question: Is it permissible to keep a small Qur'an in your wallet or car for barakah?
asked: Is it permissible to keep a small Qur'an in your wallet or car for the purposes of barakah? Isn't this similar to what other religions have done with their holy icons?
answer:
So are we allowed to keep a copy of the Qur'an in, he says, the wallet? I don't understand how the Qur'an will go in the wallet, but I guess you can get really small Qur'ans. Or, more realistically, the car, for the purposes of protecting the car.

So the answer to this actually goes back to a very theological issue, and that is: can you use the Qur'an as essentially a tamimah in Arabic, or in English a good luck charm? Can you use the Qur'an, the physical copy of the Qur'an, to bring about barakah?

Now, by unanimous consensus, you can use the Qur'an as recitation to bring about barakah. There is no ikhtilaf there. You can recite Ayat al-Kursi; you can do whatever you want with recitation of the Qur'an. The controversy, which goes back to the time of the Sahaba, is: can you use a physical written kitab of the Qur'an, a writing of the Qur'an? Can you use a written Ayat al-Kursi, can you use any type of verse, as a physical icon to bring about barakah?

We find some of the Sahaba allowed this, most famously Aisha radiallahu anha. It is authentically reported that when members of her extended family, the children and grandchildren of Asma for example, became sick, Aisha radiallahu anha would cause some verses of the Qur'an to be put around them. It is also narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As radiallahu anhu that he would allow using a physical copy of the Qur'an as a cure, a shifa. And he would say the Qur'an is a shifa, as Allah says in the Qur'an, shifa'un lima fis-sudur, whether it is recited or whether it is physically written. And it is also narrated that some of them would allow the Qur'an to be worn on the necks of children, toddlers, to protect them from the evil eye. So this is narrated from some of the Sahaba.

At the same time, it is also narrated from some of them, such as Abdullah ibn Mas'ud radiallahu anhu, that he would not allow the Qur'an to be worn as protection, and he said it is not befitting the Qur'an that it be worn as protection. So we find this little bit of controversy from the time of the Sahaba themselves: should the Qur'an be used as a physical protection or not?

Therefore, in light of this, it can be said, number one: to use a copy of the Qur'an as a physical source of blessings cannot be considered to be shirk. It's not shirk. Why? Because the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. When you seek protection from the Qur'an, you are not turning to other than Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. You can turn to the Qur'an for protection. And the Qur'an is a respected book because it contains the speech of Allah. You have to have wudu to touch it, and the physical mushaf is venerated. So it is not shirk.

But the question is: is it proper etiquette to use the Qur'an as a source of protection? Is it adab? Is it something that shows adab to the Qur'an? Some of the Sahaba said yes, some of them said no. And there is no question that the Prophet ﷺ himself did not use the physical written Qur'an, even though it was written in his lifetime. He did not use it as a physical protection.

Therefore, it is my personal opinion, I lean towards Ibn Mas'ud's position. But we cannot rebuke the other side, because who is on the other side? Aisha radiallahu anha, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As radiallahu anhu. You cannot rebuke the other side. There is legitimacy to those who say, "I want to keep a copy of the Qur'an in my glove compartment; may Allah protect my car." I'm not going to say that's wrong.

At the same time, firstly, there is no question that reciting the Qur'an and using your tongue is a higher goal in the eyes of Allah. You are actually doing an act of worship, an active one, versus keeping the Qur'an in the glove compartment, which is passive. It's not active. So there's no question that reciting the Qur'an, reciting Ayat al-Kursi, making your tongue move, every time you start the car saying "Subhan alladhi sakhkhara lana hadha", that is a higher maqam. And it is an act of worship.

Secondly, let us be honest here, and we all have either done it ourselves or have friends or relatives that do it. When you put the mushaf in the glove compartment, what happens? The glove compartment fills with miscellaneous things. It fills with the tire pressure gauge, it fills with pens and pencils. Honestly, is this adab that we are showing the Qur'an, to put it just like that on the side?

So my personal opinion is that it is not, **it's not the best thing to do**, let me phrase it that way, and you should recite the Qur'an. But I'm not going to criticize or say that it is wrong, and it is clearly not haram or shirk to do so, because turning to the Qur'an, whether it is written or whether it is recited, is an act of worship. But in my humble opinion, it is not the best mechanism of respecting the mushaf. And Allah knows best.
